subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS
messages:

Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. We had a great sync with the team and wanted to capture a couple of quick items so we can triage with finance/procurement:

1) Expected monthly token volume (rough band).
2) Peak TPS/requests per second we should plan for.
3) Budget range / target $ per 1M tokens you typically see for hosted API (ballpark).

For context: our product will do realtime summarization + search snippets across ~40K DAU in Q3. We estimate ~200K requests/day initially (mostly short prompts, average 400 tokens in + out). Very early — we need rough unit economics to model cost for the pilot.

Would appreciate a short reply with ballpark numbers and any assumptions you want us to use.

Also looping in procurement for next steps if the numbers look workable: purchasing@acmedata.com

Thanks —
Sam
Samuel Nguyen
Head of Product, Acme Data

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Nguyen <samuel.nguyen@acmedata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS

Sam —

Great to meet you on the call — appreciate the usage context. Quick post-call recap and ballpark numbers below.

Assumptions from your note:
- ~40K DAU; ~200K requests/day
- ~400 tokens per request (in + out)
- That implies ~200K * 400 = 80M tokens/day? (this looks off — I think you meant 200K requests/month?). Quick clarifying Q: is the 200K requests/day or per month?

Two scenarios depending on that:
A) If 200K requests/day (high): ~80M tokens/day -> ~2.4B tokens/month (enterprise scale). Peak TPS could be 600-800 TPS during bursts.
B) If 200K requests/month (more common for pilot): ~80M tokens/month. Peak TPS 8-15 TPS depending on distribution.

Hosted API ballparks (hosted, multi-tenant, modern open model equivalent):
- Entry tier models: $40-$70 per 1M tokens
- Mid-tier (better quality / optimized): $70-$120 per 1M tokens
- Large/very low-latency variants / premium: $120-$250 per 1M tokens

For budgeting / modeling we usually recommend using a conservative mid-tier number ($85-$100 per 1M tokens) for initial forecasts, then refine after a pilot once we have true avg tokens per request and prefix reuse.

For Dedicated or committed reserved capacity we can provide better unit economics (discounts depending on commit). Also note peak TPS drives instance sizing (and therefore committed capacity requirements) — if you expect sustained 500+ TPS we typically recommend a Dedicated capacity discussion.

Attaching a short pricing-sheet with typical bands and model examples.

Next steps:
- Quick clarification on requests/day vs month (Sam).
- If 200K/month, we can propose a pilot estimate (SOW + pricing) — Marissa from our team will follow up with a sample SOW and numbers.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Nguyen <samuel.nguyen@acmedata.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: purchasing@acmedata.com
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification: expected monthly token volume + peak TPS

Hi Sam —

Following up with the pilot estimate language and a concise set of numbers to pass to finance/procurement. Will keep this tight so you can paste into an internal doc.

Inputs (we used your "200K requests" as monthly unless you correct us):
- Requests: 200,000 / month
- Avg tokens/request (in + out): 400 tokens
- Monthly tokens = 200k * 400 = 80,000,000 tokens (~80M)
- Target modeling price: $85 / 1M tokens (hosted API, mid-tier model)
- Monthly cost = 80 * $85 = $6,800 / month
- Expected peak TPS (burst): 8-15 TPS; sustained TPS during business hours ~2-4 TPS.

Alternative (if you meant 200k/day):
- Monthly tokens ~2.4B -> monthly cost at $75-$85/1M = $180k-$204k, peak TPS 600-800 (this would be an immediate Dedicated conversation).

Notes on unit economics we typically share:
- Host model band matters: lower-quality / cheaper models can be 40-70 / 1M; best-in-class are higher. We recommended $85 as a conservative mid-tier starting point.
- Prefix caching and batching can materially reduce token usage for long-running sessions; we can help run a quick eval to estimate savings.

Attachments: pricing-sheet.pdf (pricing bands + model examples), sample SOW draft (Acme_SOW_v1.pdf).

If these numbers look reasonable, next steps from procurement:
1) We can provide a short SOW + PO-ready pricing (one page) for the pilot
2) Provide SOC 2 + security docs to your infosec (if needed)
3) Start a 30-day pilot; we can instrument token-level cost tracking in the console for transparency

Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement to walk through the SOW.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
